questions.question:
The `edge-zone` namespace runs the deployment `gateway-proxy` (label `app=gateway-proxy`). Two other namespaces exist: `internal-api` runs the deployment `orders-api` (label `app=orders-api`) exposed by the Service `orders-api-svc` on port `80`, and `corp-tools` runs the Service `legacy-svc` on port `80`.

Currently `gateway-proxy` may connect anywhere. Lock down its egress:

1. Create a NetworkPolicy named `gateway-egress` in `edge-zone` that applies ONLY to pods labeled `app=gateway-proxy`.
2. Allow egress exclusively to:
   - pods in the `internal-api` namespace on TCP port `80` (select the namespace using its `kubernetes.io/metadata.name` label)
   - DNS on port `53` (both TCP and UDP)
3. All other egress must be blocked - including `legacy-svc.corp-tools` and any external address.

Other pods in `edge-zone` must NOT be restricted by this policy.

verification.description: NetworkPolicy gateway-egress targets only app=gateway-proxy and restricts egress to internal-api plus DNS
Allowed egress to internal-api on TCP 80 (including DNS resolution) still works
Egress to corp-tools is blocked while the policy is in place

questions.question:
An external auditor ran `kube-bench` against a staging control plane and shared the raw output. The planted report is at `/tmp/exam/q2/kube-bench-results.txt`. You do NOT have access to that control plane - analyse only the provided file.

1. Extract every check with status `[FAIL]` and write the check IDs - one ID per line, e.g. `1.2.1` - to `/tmp/exam/q2/failed-checks.txt`. Do not include `PASS`, `WARN`, or `INFO` entries.
2. Check `1.2.1` failed because anonymous requests are enabled on the API server. Using the remediation section of the report, write the exact kube-apiserver flag including its required value (a single token, e.g. `--flag=value`) that remediates check `1.2.1` to `/tmp/exam/q2/remediation-1.2.1.txt`.

verification.description: failed-checks.txt lists exactly the four FAIL check IDs and nothing else
Remediation file names the correct kube-apiserver flag and value for check 1.2.1

questions.question:
Developer `dev-lena` is being onboarded and needs certificate-based, read-only pod access in the `dev-portal` namespace.

1. Under `/tmp/exam/q3/`, generate an RSA private key `dev-lena.key` and a certificate signing request `dev-lena.csr` with subject `CN=dev-lena`.
2. Create a Kubernetes `CertificateSigningRequest` named `dev-lena` for the signer `kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client` with usage `client auth`, approve it, and save the issued certificate to `/tmp/exam/q3/dev-lena.crt`.
3. Create a Role `portal-pod-reader` in `dev-portal` that allows ONLY `get`, `list`, and `watch` on `pods` and `pods/log`, and a RoleBinding `dev-lena-pod-reader` that grants it to the user `dev-lena`.

The user must NOT be able to delete pods, read secrets, or list pods in other namespaces.

verification.description: CSR dev-lena is approved and issued; the certificate is saved to disk
Role and RoleBinding grant least-privilege read access to pods only
dev-lena can read pods while destructive and secret access is denied

questions.question:
The deployment `inventory-api` in the `stock-system` namespace runs on the `default` ServiceAccount and automatically mounts a long-lived API token it never uses. The platform team wants short-lived, audience-bound tokens only.

1. Create a ServiceAccount `inventory-sa` in `stock-system` with `automountServiceAccountToken: false`.
2. Update `inventory-api` to run as `inventory-sa` and add a projected volume named `vault-token` containing a `serviceAccountToken` source with audience `internal-vault`, `expirationSeconds: 600`, and path `token`. Mount it read-only at `/var/run/vault`.
3. The default token must no longer be mounted at `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount`, and the deployment must finish its rollout.

verification.description: inventory-sa exists with automount disabled and the deployment uses it
Projected vault-token volume has the required audience, expiry, path, and read-only mount
Workload is Ready with the vault token present and the default token absent

questions.question:
A security sweep must confirm that unauthenticated users hold no extra privileges in the cluster.

1. Audit all ClusterRoleBindings and find the one - excluding the Kubernetes built-in `system:public-info-viewer` - that grants permissions to the `system:unauthenticated` group. Write its exact name as a single line to `/tmp/exam/q5/findings.txt`.
2. Delete that ClusterRoleBinding AND the custom ClusterRole it references.
3. Afterwards anonymous users (`system:anonymous` with group `system:unauthenticated`) must NOT be able to read secrets, and legitimate bindings - the built-in `system:public-info-viewer` and the `release-bot-read` binding used by the release tooling - must remain untouched.

verification.description: The offending ClusterRoleBinding is correctly identified in findings.txt
Binding and custom ClusterRole removed; anonymous secret access is denied
Legitimate bindings survive the cleanup

questions.question:
The deployment `host-inspector` in the `node-ops` namespace was built by a former contractor. It runs with `hostNetwork: true`, `hostPID: true`, and mounts the node root filesystem through a `hostPath` volume - far more host access than it needs.

Harden the deployment so that:

1. `hostNetwork`, `hostPID`, and ALL `hostPath` volumes are removed.
2. The container runs with `runAsNonRoot: true` and `runAsUser: 10001`.
3. The container sets `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, drops ALL capabilities, and uses `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`.
4. The deployment completes its rollout and the pod runs with its own pod IP (not a node IP).

verification.description: Host namespaces and hostPath volumes are gone from host-inspector
Hardened securityContext is enforced (non-root, no escalation, read-only root, no capabilities)
Deployment is Ready and the pod runs off the host network

questions.question:
**SIMULATED TASK** - this exercise analyses planted evidence files only; there is no live host to change and you must not modify any node.

An ops engineer captured the state of a Kubernetes worker node before it is allowed into production:

- `/tmp/exam/q7/enabled-services.txt` - output of `systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled`
- `/tmp/exam/q7/listening-ports.txt` - output of `ss -tlnp`

The node security baseline permits ONLY these enabled units: `sshd.service`, `containerd.service`, `kubelet.service`, `cron.service`, `dbus.service`, and `systemd-*` units.

1. Write the exact names of every enabled unit that violates the baseline - one unit name per line, nothing else - to `/tmp/exam/q7/disable-list.txt`.
2. One listening socket belongs to a container runtime daemon exposing its remote API without authentication. Write that port number (digits only) to `/tmp/exam/q7/insecure-api.txt`.

verification.description: disable-list.txt names exactly the units violating the baseline
The unauthenticated container-runtime API port is identified

questions.question:
The deployment `checkout-api` in the `checkout` namespace is stuck: its pod fails with `CreateContainerConfigError` because compliance enforces `runAsNonRoot: true` but the image `nginx:1.27-alpine` starts as root.

Fix the workload WITHOUT weakening the policy:

1. `runAsNonRoot: true` must remain enforced - do not remove or disable it.
2. Switch the container image to the approved non-root build `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27-alpine` (it listens on port `8080`).
3. Update the container port to `8080` and the Service `checkout-svc` so its `targetPort` is `8080` (keep the Service port at `80`).
4. The deployment must become Ready, the container process must run as a non-root UID, and `checkout-svc` must answer HTTP requests from inside the namespace.

verification.description: runAsNonRoot is still enforced and the approved non-root image is in use
checkout-api is Ready and the container runs as a non-root UID
checkout-svc routes to port 8080 and answers HTTP requests

questions.question:
Traffic between the payments client and the orders backend in the `intra-tls` namespace currently flows over plain HTTP. A certificate has been issued at `/tmp/exam/q9/orders.crt` with its key at `/tmp/exam/q9/orders.key`, and the prepared nginx TLS server configuration already exists in the ConfigMap `orders-tls-conf` (it serves HTTPS on container port `8443` using certificates from `/etc/nginx/tls/`).

Encrypt the connection:

1. Create a TLS Secret named `orders-tls` in `intra-tls` from the issued certificate and key.
2. Update the deployment `orders-app`: mount the Secret at `/etc/nginx/tls` and the ConfigMap `orders-tls-conf` at `/etc/nginx/conf.d`.
3. Update the Service `orders-svc` to expose port `443` with `targetPort: 8443` (replace the old port 80 mapping).
4. Verify from the `payments-client` pod that `curl -k https://orders-svc.intra-tls.svc` returns the orders response.

verification.description: TLS secret orders-tls is created from the issued certificate
orders-app mounts the certificate and TLS server config and is Ready
HTTPS served through orders-svc is reachable from payments-client

questions.question:
Namespaces labeled `volume-policy=restricted` (the `storage-guard` namespace already carries this label) must refuse any pod that mounts a `hostPath` volume.

Using CEL-based admission control:

1. Create a `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` named `deny-hostpath` that matches pod CREATE and UPDATE operations and rejects pods declaring any `hostPath` volume.
2. Create a `ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding` named `deny-hostpath-binding` with validation action `Deny`, bound to namespaces labeled `volume-policy=restricted`.
3. Demonstrate the policy: attempt to create a pod with a `hostPath` volume in `storage-guard` and capture the API server rejection message to `/tmp/exam/q10/rejected.txt`.
4. Create a compliant pod named `safe-cache` in `storage-guard` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 86400`) that uses an `emptyDir` volume named `cache` mounted at `/cache`. It must reach `Running`.

verification.description: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and binding exist and target restricted namespaces with Deny
hostPath pods are rejected by the live policy and the rejection was captured
Compliant pod safe-cache runs with emptyDir storage

questions.question:
The release team received a third-party deployment manifest at `/tmp/exam/q11/webhook-deploy.yaml`. It is dangerously misconfigured (privileged, host PID, unpinned image).

1. Scan the manifest with trivy and save the report: `trivy config /tmp/exam/q11/webhook-deploy.yaml -o /tmp/exam/q11/trivy-report.txt` (network access may be needed for the checks bundle).
2. Write a hardened copy to `/tmp/exam/q11/webhook-deploy-fixed.yaml` that keeps the same Deployment name, namespace, and labels but:
   - pins the image to `busybox:1.36`
   - removes `privileged` and `hostPID`
   - sets `runAsNonRoot: true` and `runAsUser: 10001`
   - sets `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, drops ALL capabilities, and sets `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`
   - adds cpu/memory requests and limits (any sane values)
3. Score the hardened manifest: `kubesec scan /tmp/exam/q11/webhook-deploy-fixed.yaml > /tmp/exam/q11/kubesec-report.json` - the score must be at least `5`.
4. Apply the hardened manifest; the deployment `webhook-gw` in `release-engineering` must become Ready.

verification.description: Scan reports exist for the insecure manifest and the hardened copy
Hardened manifest meets every checklist item and reaches the kubesec score threshold
Hardened deployment is applied to the cluster and Ready

questions.question:
The deployment `web-frontend` in the `release-pinning` namespace references its image by the mutable tag `nginx:1.27-alpine`. Supply-chain policy requires immutable digest references so the running artifact can never silently change.

1. Resolve the exact digest of `nginx:1.27-alpine` - for example from the running pod's `.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID` - and write the full pinned reference in the form `nginx@sha256:<64-hex-digits>` as a single line to `/tmp/exam/q12/pinned-image.txt`.
2. Update `web-frontend` to use that digest-pinned reference instead of the tag.
3. The rollout must complete and the running container's `imageID` must match the digest you pinned.

verification.description: A valid digest-pinned reference is recorded in pinned-image.txt
web-frontend uses the digest-pinned image reference from the answer file
Rollout is complete and the running image matches the pinned digest

questions.question:
The deployment `web-api` in the `sbom-audit` namespace still runs `nginx:1.25-alpine`. Before approving an upgrade, the security team needs a software inventory and a vulnerability picture of the old image.

1. Generate a CycloneDX JSON SBOM for `nginx:1.25-alpine` with syft: `syft nginx:1.25-alpine -o cyclonedx-json=/tmp/exam/q13/sbom.json`.
2. Scan that SBOM with trivy and save JSON output: `trivy sbom /tmp/exam/q13/sbom.json --format json -o /tmp/exam/q13/sbom-vulns.json`.
3. From the SBOM, extract the exact version of the `nginx` component and write it (version only, e.g. `1.2.3`) to `/tmp/exam/q13/nginx-version.txt`.
4. Upgrade the deployment `web-api` to `nginx:1.27-alpine` and wait for the rollout to finish.

verification.description: CycloneDX SBOM for nginx:1.25-alpine is generated and contains components
SBOM vulnerability scan is saved and the nginx version was extracted
web-api is upgraded to nginx:1.27-alpine and Ready

questions.question:
**SIMULATED TASK** - the current cluster backend cannot load an audit policy, so this file will NOT be applied; do not modify the live API server. Write the policy file only.

Create an API server audit policy at `/tmp/exam/q14/audit-policy.yaml` (`apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1`, `kind: Policy`) that satisfies ALL of the following, with the rules in exactly this order:

1. The `RequestReceived` stage must not be logged for any rule (use `omitStages` at the policy level).
2. Rule 1: requests touching `secrets` (core API group) are logged at `RequestResponse` level.
3. Rule 2: `watch` requests by the user `system:kube-proxy` on `endpoints` and `services` (core API group) are NOT logged (`None`).
4. Rule 3: `create` requests to the `pods/exec` subresource (core API group) are logged at `RequestResponse` level.
5. Rule 4 (last): everything else is logged at `Metadata` level - a catch-all rule with no resource or user filter.

`yq` is available on this machine for checking your YAML.

verification.description: Audit policy file is valid audit.k8s.io/v1 Policy YAML with omitStages set
Secrets are logged at RequestResponse first and the catch-all Metadata rule is last
kube-proxy watch exclusion and pods/exec auditing rules are present in order

questions.question:
The SOC flagged unusual outbound traffic from the `batch-ops` namespace, which runs three CronJobs: `db-backup`, `report-gen`, and `cache-warm`. One of them was tampered with: it downloads and executes a remote payload and runs under a ServiceAccount that can read secrets cluster-wide.

1. Investigate the CronJob specs. Write the name of the malicious CronJob on line 1 and the IP address it contacts on line 2 of `/tmp/exam/q15/findings.txt`.
2. Contain it: suspend ONLY the malicious CronJob (`spec.suspend: true`). The two legitimate CronJobs must keep running unsuspended.
3. Revoke its excessive privileges: delete the ClusterRoleBinding and ClusterRole that give the `ops-runner` ServiceAccount cluster-wide secret access. Afterwards `ops-runner` must NOT be able to read secrets in any namespace.

verification.description: Malicious CronJob and its exfiltration endpoint are identified
Only the malicious CronJob is suspended; legitimate jobs keep running
Cluster-wide secret access for ops-runner is revoked

questions.question:
A code review suspects the deployment `notify-bot` in the `notify` namespace prints its API credential to stdout at startup, exposing it to anyone who can read logs.

1. Inspect the pod logs in `notify`, recover the leaked credential value, and write it (the token value only) to `/tmp/exam/q16/leaked-token.txt`.
2. Rotate the credential: update the Secret `notify-token` so the `token` key holds the replacement value issued by the platform team: `ntfy_c4f1e8b2d7a0`.
3. Fix the workload so the token value is never logged again: the startup message must read exactly `startup: token loaded` (no environment interpolation of the token), then restart/roll out the deployment so the running pod uses the rotated secret.

When done, the current pod logs must contain `startup: token loaded` and must NOT contain any token value.

verification.description: Leaked credential recovered from the pod logs
Secret rotated and the running pod uses the new token
Startup logging no longer exposes any token value
